human_readable: Revival of Hebrew as a Living Language
summary: KERNEL CONTEST: The commitment 'Hebrew is a living language' was held under sharply different readings across two millennia. Under a liturgical-only reading the kernel was occupied but dormant. Under a native-daily reading it was reconstructed into ordinary speech in the late 19th-20th c. The contest is whether reciting a preserved symbol counts as occupying the kernel, or whether only native generation does. Library verdict context: D1 strict-reachability break.

human_readable: Renaissance Reconstruction of Classical Latin
summary: KERNEL CONTEST: 'Correct Latin' read one way by medieval users (a living drifted vernacular) and another by humanist reconstructors (the Classical form recovered from texts, no living practitioners). The contest is whether the reconstructed form was reachable from the drifted one or a separate kernel reoccupied from a symbol. D1 break.

Tests coherent-multi-reading vs incoherent-bundle directly.
